transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
My head has been feeling foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I’ve already called.
Have you been feeling persistently down or depressed lately?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed, no. I’ve mostly just noticed this fogginess and getting mixed up.
Are these mix-ups interfering with your ability to manage everyday tasks on your own, like paying bills, taking medications, or preparing meals?

Yes. I’ve missed doctor visits, and I got the senior center schedule so tangled up that my husband has had to take over the calls and calendars. Even repair decisions I used to handle myself, I’ve needed his help with.
Did these difficulties develop slowly and gradually over time, or did they seem to start suddenly?
It started about four months ago, around when the water damage forced us into the remodel.
Have you noticed that these difficulties have gotten worse in sudden steps or drops?
I’m not sure what you mean by sudden steps. I just know I’ve been having more trouble since all of that started.
Have you ever had a stroke or a mini-stroke?
I’m not sure. No one has ever told me I had one.
Have you ever experienced sudden weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed one side of my body suddenly going weak or numb.
Have you seen things that other people could not see, such as figures, animals, or objects?
No, I haven’t noticed seeing things that other people couldn’t see.
Have you noticed any involuntary shaking or trembling in your hands or arms?
I haven’t really noticed any shaking or trembling in my hands or arms.
Since this began four months ago, have your memory problems been getting steadily worse over time?
Yes, I think it has been getting worse. My head feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, even which volunteer I already called.
Have you had any trouble finding the right words when you are speaking?
I’m not sure. Sometimes I have to stop and think, but I can usually get the words out.
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your mood or personality, such as becoming unusually irritable or losing interest in things?
Yes… I’ve lost interest in things I used to love. My watercolors, my tomato plants, line dancing, even watching the cardinals out back—they just sit there now, and I can’t seem to make myself care.
Looking back, were you experiencing any of these memory or thinking difficulties before the remodel started four months ago?
No, not that I can remember. It started about four months ago, when the water damage led to the remodel.
When these memory issues first began four months ago, did they start gradually and slowly worsen, or did they appear quite suddenly?
I’m not really sure. I just know it was around that time, but I can’t say whether it came on all at once or slowly.
Has your husband or anyone close to you mentioned noticing any memory slips or changes before four months ago?
I don’t think so. What’s been bothering me is this foggy feeling—I keep mixing up simple things, like appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I’ve already called.
Has anyone in your biological family, such as a parent or sibling, ever been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or another form of dementia?
I’m not sure about that. I don’t recall anyone in my family being diagnosed with it.
Have you had a brain scan, such as a CT or MRI, to check for causes of your memory problems?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember having a CT or MRI for this.
Have you had any blood tests recently to check for other causes of your memory problems, such as a thyroid issue or vitamin deficiency?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember having any blood tests recently for that.
Has a doctor or memory specialist ever formally diagnosed you with Alzheimer's disease?
I don’t believe so. I can’t remember anyone telling me I was formally diagnosed with that.
